Author: @Velociraptor_mania
Content:
It's rare for me to get scared by a horror game, resident evil, fnaf, bendy, silent hill. I get creeped out by them for sure. However, none of them, has ever made me feel TRUE horror like this....even just by watching Cory's I'm feeling so jumpy and paranoid, I'm suddenly aware of my surroundings and feel startled by the slightest noise. Even with Cory is opening the door to the apartment, I get so scared that something, or someone, might be at the other side. I think what sets this game apart from the other horror games, is that this, could happen in real life. It just doesn't apply to pop stars or celebs. Chillart's previous games have shown that even regular people can and have experience something like this before. when you're playing your typical horror game, it doesn't hit as hard because at the end of the day you know they are fiction, you know something like Bendy couldn't happened. But here.

 True horror, is when you know it could happen to you in real life.

The game really does do a good job of making _everyone_ seem against you, and it turns out to be warranted because a large portion of the characters were.

Brilliant how if you go back and look, every one of the conspirators was trying to keep you isolated and away from positive influences and outside lifelines. Asuka despite seeming suspicious didn't do anything resembling that, she was just generally thoughtless and that was why they used her against you. They wanted you paranoid, and to manipulate that paranoia into getting with Rikiya. 

You could take it as the only way to win is really to trust someone, conversely the only person not feeding into your distrust of others, Asuka. Or you could interpret it as them underestimating how good of a survival instinct her paranoia was, their little narrative fell apart because she didn't take anything at face value, not even stuff that would confirm her fears.

Author: @viablos455
Content:
i said this before in a reply somewhere but i wanted to make a full-blown comment about this amazing game.

i've been in a toxic/abusive relationship before and i wanted to state the game does a good job at giving its players a similar experience.

the game also does an AMAZING job at "edging" us for help, where we actually never receive satisfactory assistance until the last second - when nina gets "rescued" from the stalker by her ex and the cop - so that when we DO get that help, that single satisfying help, we take it blindly and hang onto it. its a really great and i guess safe experience for people to experience the phenomenon of love bombing, touch starvation in toxic relationships, etc. in a weird way to understand what its like being a victim, where that one major catalyst of good kind of keeps us stuck in that toxic/abusive relationship. its a proven manipulation tactics that happen in many abusive/toxic relationships.

i feel like cory's response, to how he stated he would immediately marry the dude, is actually very much a victim-like response in this situation, where we're so blinded by that one notion of hope/love/save that it makes us want to stay still. he never questioned why his ex came alongside the cop when he got to his first ending! his reaction, is by far, extremely normal, and a very sad reality that happens. notice how nina got back with the ex after that, and cory's commitment to marry him!

Author: @acearohippo
Content:
The true ending made me feel so validated because I'd been suspicious of all them with each intro, except Asuka. From the police randomly running up to her inquiring if she was alone (which Cory caught, but didn't follow through with) and then later giving her his personal number, to the building manager giving away her personal number right after the face reveal scene (again, Cory sort of caught that it was weird for a building manager to not introduce themselves sooner), and the ex was just automatically suspicious because he's her ex and if she broke up with him AND had him blocked (also, kudos to the shopkeeper for protecting her by blocking him!), it was probably for good reason. Now, I didn't think it was a four way planned trick to... what, get her to take her ex back? I just thought there was going to be multiple endings of her dealing with the reality of different types of stalkers.

And I trusted Asuka fully with that message about calling the police.  Honestly, my first instinct when MC asked about calling the police was an emphatic "NO!" but that's because I was of the mind that the stalker had her house bugged and her calling the police would cause him to come zooming back in and stabbing her. But then she explained about it being night time and going in person so that they take he more seriously as well as it being broad daylight (less likely to be attacked) and all I could think was "Oh my goodness... a video game npc that actually uses sound reasoning". I would trust Asuka with my life.

Author: @noactualreasontolive
Content:
Dude, watching this whole game was so surreal, even though I am male. I could oddly relate to all this because I am a paranoid schizophrenic. While I am medicated, many times I just happen to skip the prescribed doses out of a bad mood or if something specific happens that day. For example a priest walking past me on the street. 

But this whole gameplay reminded me, in a somewhat unpleasant way, that most people don't ever feel this scared on the norm. Usually you can trust your family or friends and neighbors.

The way this game was structured, I just felt like I was watching one of my bad days through the eyes of someone else.
Everytime a stranger comes near me during those times when I'm off my meds, even without them talking, I feel scared, I feel as if they know where I live. I'm claustrophobic due to that. If I'm in a closed space with someone else, even acquaintance, I freak out horribly. Because I become incapable of thinking logically, I just get a strong gut feeling that almost makes me hit the other person in an attempt to be safe. More so when the opposite sex is said stranger.

Author: @ApexPredator1000
Content:
We all develop Parasocial relationships; it's a natural human reaction in our need for connection - we connect with fictional characters and artists through our entertainment mediums, even though we know it's only one-way. Case in point, my brother and I were watching the video, and we both responded at one point, to Cory's question "Did you see him there?!" with "Really??" like we expected him to respond back (I've never done this before haha). 

But as with all things - it's moderation and self control. Parasocial Relationships becomes dangerous when people take things too far, and get too attached. We see it with 'toxic fanbases' for fictional characters (shipping wars, and which character would win in a fight etc.) and in the case of real people, it can result in these 'stalker fans' at the worst end of the spectrum, where they truly believe they have a real relationship with people. That's why, on top of these passive hobbies & entertainment, it's good to balance with active hobbies (creative works, exercise) and developing real relationships to keep our minds healthy and realities grounded, and to help those that struggle with this, rather than judge them. Keep the fun and stay safe all!
